title: Implement typed ClientNode v6 activation atomics
description: Provide a target-validated, unsafe-to-construct typed view over pw_node_activation with legal ClientNode v6 readiness, trigger, claim, finish, pending, result, and timing operations. Default crate builds must not depend on a developer source checkout or executing target binaries; upstream private-header comparison remains opt-in developer validation.
acceptance_criteria: Supported target ABIs are explicit and validated; normal and cross builds do not require HOME or PIPEWIRE_SOURCE_DIR; activation access forms no whole-record Rust reference; legal transitions use matching atomics; invalid size/alignment/version/state fail; upstream C differential checks are reproducible when explicitly enabled; node tests and clippy pass.
close_reason: Implemented unsafe-to-construct ActivationView with x86_64 Linux ABI constants, SeqCst v6 readiness/trigger/claim/finish/pending/result operations, validation and differential tests. Normal builds are source-independent and pass with HOME and PIPEWIRE_SOURCE_DIR unset; private-header comparison is opt-in via node/tools.

title: Give AddMem one ownership-safe importer
description: Replace multicast owning RawFd delivery with one connection-level importer receiving OwnedFd. Define duplicate IDs, RemoveMem, frame decode failure, importer failure, disconnect, active mapping, and descriptor cleanup semantics.
acceptance_criteria: AddMem transfers one OwnedFd to exactly one memory owner; ordinary listeners cannot observe an owning raw descriptor; RemoveMem and disconnect close resources exactly once; malformed or unsupported events cannot shift descriptors to later frames; lifecycle and /proc/self/fd tests pass.
notes:
Client inbound AddMem now takes one frame-local OwnedFd through CoreMemoryImporter (28493dc5), releases importer on teardown (a1b6c27b), and canonical scripted AddMem plus wrong-index/no-named-memfd-leak coverage landed in 63bb6b63. Remaining acceptance gap is an explicit scripted RemoveMem action/test with active mapping lifecycle and baseline /proc/self/fd accounting.
Explicit scripted RemoveMem lifecycle and named memfd closure landed in 52f006af; importer callback/replacement/drop lock safety landed in 9fe61ecf. Remaining policy/test gaps are duplicate IDs, importer failure handling, and exact baseline /proc/self/fd accounting across repeated cycles.
close_reason: Completed across 28493dc5, a1b6c27b, 9fe61ecf, 52f006af, 86cc4b9b, and 8d0ab085: one frame-local OwnedFd importer, canonical AddMem/RemoveMem, lock-safe callbacks/drop, generational node MemoryPool, Core adapter, duplicate/unsupported/wrong-index failures, later-frame isolation, disconnect cleanup, and repeated fd-baseline tests.

title: Implement complete native frames with owned descriptors
description: Implement the accepted canonical frame transport interface for incremental Unix stream IO and SCM_RIGHTS. Payload bytes and exact descriptors form one ownership unit; frame consumption is independent of typed dispatch; send supports partial writes while ancillary data is emitted once.
acceptance_criteria: Client and scripted-peer paths can consume the same frame interface; every header and payload split, frame coalescing, EINTR, EAGAIN, IN-with-HUP, partial send, descriptor count mismatch, ancillary truncation, unknown object, and disconnect-mid-frame behavior is bounded and tested without FD leaks.
notes:
Shared crate plus all consumer migrations are complete: client outbound f8a1eb94, scripted peer ad51b892, client inbound 28493dc5/a1b6c27b, canonical scripted AddMem 63bb6b63. Remaining acceptance gap is deterministic EINTR syscall injection/coverage; all other listed segmentation, coalescing, EAGAIN/HUP, partial send, FD mismatch/truncation, unknown-object, and disconnect cleanup paths are tested.
Independent review follow-ups landed: stateful public packet reader e8f64a63, visible ancillary cleanup and sender-local limits 70c87ebe, terminal client frame/socket/FD cleanup 66b06101. Strict workspace clippy, deterministic workspace tests, formatting, and frame tests pass. EINTR injection remains open.

title: Repair SPA plugin ABI and ownership chains
description: Correct SPA plugin C vtable ABIs and represent Plugin-to-factory and handle-to-interface ownership so dynamic library or handle drop cannot leave live raw-pointer wrappers. Ground layouts and calling conventions in local upstream headers and add focused lifecycle verification.
acceptance_criteria: C function pointers use the confirmed extern C ABI; factories retain their plugin library owner; interfaces retain or borrow their handle owner; relevant drop orders cannot unload or clear live pointers; SPA tests and clippy pass, with unresolved adjacent FFI risks documented.
notes: Delegated for a bounded upstream-grounded implementation; agent may commit a repair design if ownership changes cannot be completed safely in one coherent change.
close_reason: Completed in 3d9e77db and 2af3cbce: C ABIs and constness corrected, plugin/handle/interface ownership retained, failed-init cleanup and drop order tested, ABI errors/null metadata propagate through Result instead of wrapping invalid pointers.

title: Make imported memory mappings bounds-safe
description: Harden node shared-memory mapping with checked ranges, backing-file size validation, page-aligned physical mappings and logical subranges, correct unmapping, and explicit concurrent truncation/revocation policy.
acceptance_criteria: Valid unaligned logical ranges map correctly; zero, overflow, beyond-EOF, and invalid backing ranges fail before slice exposure; munmap uses the physical base and length; focused node tests and clippy pass; residual truncation risk is documented.
notes: Delegated for implementation from the architecture re-kickoff; edits restricted to node shared-memory code and tests.
close_reason: Completed across f590a129, 53068b7d, and 36d81512: checked/aligned mappings and unmapping, size/seal policy, Send-not-Sync traits, unsafe shared-byte access contract propagated through transport/runtime, and negative/compile tests.

title: Make SPA POD decoding total over bytes
description: Harden SPA POD decode and parser entry points against truncated headers and bodies, zero child sizes, undersized arrays/objects, checked-arithmetic failures, invalid choices, hangs, and peer-sized allocation hazards. Preserve discovered hostile inputs as regression tests and establish a fuzzing entry point.
acceptance_criteria: Arbitrary implemented POD inputs return a value or bounded error without panic, infinite loop, arithmetic overflow, or unbounded allocation; known review cases have regression tests; focused SPA tests and clippy pass.
notes: Delegated for implementation from the architecture re-kickoff; focused on spa/src/pod and negative tests.
close_reason: Completed across 5149c56d, b2e94f13, and 770c2e0c: checked POD size/progress arithmetic, malformed-shape regressions, deterministic generated-byte coverage, and a persistent 64 KiB-bounded cargo-fuzz harness with structured corpus seeds.

title: Add parameterized subsystem stress and hyperfine harness
description: Build a composable DI-like harness where deterministic scenarios, production subsystem executors, verification, load policy, and reporting can be reused by fast correctness tests and release-mode hyperfine workloads. Cover frame transport, complex SPA POD batches, and generational session memory with named presets and granular overrides.
acceptance_criteria: Small end-to-end tests pass for every workload; runners validate checked parameters and deterministic checksums/state; hyperfine benchmarks release binaries directly with configurable matrices and JSON output; smoke hyperfine executes successfully; documentation explains extension, reproducibility, and resource bounds.
notes: Delegated as one coherent stress/ implementation: reusable scenario/executor/verifier/load components, frame/POD/memory workloads, preset and override CLI, release-mode hyperfine matrix, tests, and smoke benchmark.

title: Preserve generation and unknown-event compatibility
description: Correct session-layer behavior above complete frame ownership: apply inbound generation footers before callbacks can synchronously reply, commit outbound generation only after encoding/enqueue succeeds, and consume unknown object/opcode frames without terminating an otherwise synchronized connection.
acceptance_criteria: Generation-bearing Ping produces Pong with the current generation; queue/encode rejection does not advance last-sent generation; unknown object and opcode frames with FDs are dropped exactly once while a following valid frame dispatches; malformed semantic payload policy is explicit and tested.
notes: Implementation delegated after frame review: inbound generation-before-callback, outbound generation commit-after-enqueue, and unknown-opcode continuation with focused tests.
close_reason: Completed in 5efed7ce: validated inbound generation applies before callbacks, outbound generation commits only after successful enqueue, and FD-bearing unknown opcodes are consumed frame-locally while following valid events dispatch. Focused tests, client integration, clippy, and formatting pass.

title: Define and enforce the threading contract
description: Inventory blanket unsafe Send/Sync assertions, actual event-loop affinity, SPA C interface requirements, and cross-thread callers. Design a compile-safe migration to compiler-derived auto traits and explicit cross-thread command handles, then implement it in bounded changes.
acceptance_criteria: An upstream- and code-grounded threading contract inventories unsafe traits and affinity; migration commits remove blanket assertions where possible; invalid cross-thread use has compile-time coverage; remaining unsafe implementations have local documented invariants and concurrency tests.
notes:
Delegated for a code-wide inventory and implementation-ready threading contract before unsafe trait removal begins.
Threading contract committed at /.design/threading-contract/threading0.gpt56.md (77933fdd). Low-risk MappedRegion and SendablePtr Sync removals plus compile assertions landed in 53068b7d. Remaining work is loop-local ownership, bounded generation-aware handles, browser migration, refcounted macro trait removal, and generic plugin trait narrowing.

title: Make listener dispatch reentrancy-safe
description: Stop invoking user callbacks while holding the hook-list mutation lock. Define ordering and mutation semantics for self-removal, listener addition, and nested emission while preserving FnMut callbacks and existing proxy behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Self-removal and listener addition during dispatch cannot deadlock or invalidate iteration; ordering semantics are documented by tests; supported nested behavior is explicit; SPA tests and clippy pass without broad proxy churn.
notes: Delegated for a minimal tested dispatch policy in spa hook code.
close_reason: Completed in f7b2f807 and ddda0998: callbacks execute outside the list mutex; self-removal/addition/nested emission are defined; concurrent external emissions serialize without drops; poison-safe restoration and panic/removal/concurrency tests pass.

title: Bound integration-test waits with diagnostics
description: Prevent scripted-peer accept/read operations and real-daemon integration paths from hanging indefinitely. Add reusable deadlines or socket timeouts, replace avoidable startup sleeps, and report the last protocol step and relevant state on timeout.
acceptance_criteria: Tests prove stalled accept/read and daemon startup/completion fail within configured bounds with actionable diagnostics; deterministic happy paths remain green; no integration test can wait forever on external process or socket progress.
notes: Delegated for bounded scripted-peer and real-daemon test waits with focused timeout regression coverage.
close_reason: Completed in 91c481b2: scripted accept/read/write deadlines with step diagnostics, bounded connect/completion helpers, bounded AddMem/main-loop waits, and daemon readiness/process-group cleanup. Host callback stalls now fail boundedly and reap helpers.

title: Prove one deterministic ClientNode process cycle
description: Extend the scripted peer to configure one output ClientNode using real memfd-backed activation and media buffers plus real trigger/completion eventfds. Execute one typed process callback, verify output bytes and state, then exercise cleanup.
acceptance_criteria: The peer observes the expected output bytes, activation/chunk transitions, and completion count; callback borrows cannot escape the cycle; RemoveMem and disconnect terminate worker state and mappings; descriptor accounting returns to baseline; the scenario has explicit deadlines and diagnostics.

title: Model one typed ClientNode session
description: Replace the single pending transport accumulator with a per-ClientNode transition system using connection-wide exported memory and per-node transport generation, activation, negotiated format, port IO, buffers, cycle borrows, reconfiguration, and teardown.
acceptance_criteria: One output-node session accepts supported valid event orderings, rejects invalid transitions with typed errors, preserves retryable state, invalidates revoked resources deterministically, and exposes a ready state whose process callback receives typed cycle-scoped buffers rather than raw activation bytes.
notes:
Typed data-plane foundations landed: activation v1 atomics 82a042ac/c7530ef2 and synchronous SPA_IO_Buffers/spa_chunk/output publication 44c09215. Remaining implementation is connection MemoryPool, per-node generations/configurator, metadata/multi-plane assembly, peer activation, cycle owner, retirement/teardown, and runtime adapter migration.
Core-to-MemoryPool adapter landed in 8d0ab085. Scripted Core AddMem/RemoveMem now drives the generational pool, and duplicate/unsupported/wrong-index failures prove candidate closure, later-frame isolation, and terminal cleanup. Memory importer ticket is closed; next is per-node ClientNode configuration over this handle.

title: Implement the minimum ClientNode wire surface
description: Inventory upstream ClientNode traffic for one output node and implement only the typed methods/events needed for transport, activation, port IO, buffers, activation state, processing, and teardown. Generate or centralize opcodes and wire DTOs rather than adding parallel constants.
acceptance_criteria: The scripted peer and client share canonical definitions for the selected ClientNode messages; valid messages round-trip or differentially match upstream; malformed payloads fail safely; object construction and dispatch support ClientNode without raw application parsing.

title: Prove one ownership-safe ClientNode cycle
description: Deliver the architecture re-kickoff tracer bullet documented in /.design/architecture-review/review-rekick0.oc.md: bounded protocol decoding, frame-owned descriptors, ownership-safe memory import, typed per-node activation and buffer state, one deterministic process cycle, and WAV playback through the same path. This supersedes the narrower server-unification architecture because protocol sharing is a means to the ClientNode outcome rather than the product goal.
acceptance_criteria: A scripted native peer configures one output ClientNode using real memfd and eventfd resources; the callback receives a cycle-scoped typed output buffer, writes verified bytes, signals completion, and tears down without leaks. POD/frame inputs are bounded, AddMem has one OwnedFd owner, tests have deadlines, and the same interfaces support WAV playback.

title: Replace NativeHeader with marshal Header in server/
description:
Once Header is public, replace `server/src/protocol/frame.rs::NativeHeader` with `pipewire_native::protocol::marshal::message::Header`.

Field mapping: `NativeHeader.object_id` → `Header.id`, `NativeHeader.payload_size` → `Header.size`, rest identical.

Also update `NativePacket` to use the shared Header. Keep `NativePacket` itself in server — it's a simpler server-specific wrapper (no footer, no generics) vs the client's `Message<T, F>`.

Update server/Cargo.toml to add `pipewire-native` dependency.
acceptance_criteria:
- `NativeHeader` is deleted from server/
- `NativePacket` uses `pipewire_native::...::Header`
- All server tests pass
- No duplicate header encode/decode logic
close_reason: Superseded by shared frame transport. The scripted peer's packet adapter now delegates to pipewire-native-protocol Header and contains no independent header or SCM_RIGHTS implementation.

title: Add pipewire-native dependency to server crate
description:
Currently server/ only depends on `pipewire-native-spa` and `libc`. To reuse any protocol types from pipewire/, server/Cargo.toml needs `pipewire-native` as a dependency.

Check for circular dependency issues — pipewire/ already has `pipewire-native-server` as a *dev-dependency*, so a regular dependency the other way should be fine (dev-deps don't create cycles for normal builds).

This is a prerequisite for SU-replace-header and SU-pub-opcodes.
acceptance_criteria:
- `pipewire-native.workspace = true` added to `server/Cargo.toml` `[dependencies]`
- `cargo check --workspace` passes with no circular dependency errors
close_reason: Superseded by pipewire-native-protocol. The scripted peer now depends on the narrow protocol crate rather than the full client crate, avoiding the proposed reverse dependency.

title: Make marshal::message::Header and constants public
description:
Change `pub(crate)` to `pub` for:
- `marshal::message::Header` struct and all its fields
- `marshal::HEADER_LEN` constant
- `marshal::mod` module itself (it's currently `pub(crate)`)

Then in `pipewire/src/protocol/mod.rs`, re-export these types publicly so server can `use pipewire_native::protocol::marshal::message::Header`.

This is the gate for all other unification work — until the types are visible, server cannot use them.
acceptance_criteria:
- `Header`, its fields, and `HEADER_LEN` are `pub`
- `pipewire/src/protocol/mod.rs` has a public re-export path
- server/ can `use pipewire_native::protocol::...::Header`
- `cargo check --workspace` passes
close_reason: Superseded by the public Header in pipewire-native-protocol. The full client marshal module remains private rather than being widened for test infrastructure.

title: Server/Pipewire Protocol Unification
description:
Eliminate protocol type duplication between `server/` and `pipewire/src/protocol/marshal/`. The server crate independently reimplements wire types (Header, opcodes, SCM_RIGHTS I/O, POD helpers) that already exist in pipewire/.

Root cause: everything in `pipewire/src/protocol/marshal/` is `pub(crate)`, so the server crate cannot use any of it despite being in the same workspace.

Strategy: progressively widen visibility of wire-format types, starting with the highest-value lowest-risk items (Header, constants), then move to shared I/O and POD helpers. The `Marshallable` trait and `PairList` can eventually support server-side decode-by-header dispatch.

Architecture: Option B from the analysis (re-export from pipewire/ with a feature flag or public submodule) is the right first step. Extracting a separate crate (Option A) can be revisited later if the boundary becomes clearer.
close_reason: Superseded by SU-client-node-cycle. Shared transport now lives in pipewire-native-protocol and both scripted-peer directions plus client outbound consume it; broad client-marshal publication and server reverse dependency are no longer current architecture.

title: Play WAV audio through the typed ClientNode path
description: Replace the WAV-player integration sketch with adapter-node creation, explicit format negotiation, cycle-scoped output-buffer filling, chunk metadata, underrun/end-of-stream behavior, and coordinated PipeWire/process-runtime shutdown using the same path proven by the deterministic cycle test.
acceptance_criteria: The example has no raw activation/buffer integration TODO, rejects unsupported WAV/negotiated formats clearly, produces audible output against a real daemon, shuts down cleanly, and does not use example-only ownership or transport shortcuts.

title: Extract and publish opcode constants from Marshallable enums
acceptance_criteria:
- Opcode constants are defined once and shared
- Server's opcode modules deleted or replaced with re-exports
- No risk of opcode mismatch between client and server
close_reason: Superseded by the shared protocol crate and future canonical ClientNode/core wire DTOs. Server-local opcode duplication will be removed through consumer migration rather than publishing client marshal enums.

title: Move spa_data_type constants to the spa crate
description:
Server defines `spa_data_type` constants (INVALID, MEM_PTR, MEM_FD, DMA_BUF, MEM_ID, SYNC_OBJ) which belong in the spa crate alongside other SPA enum definitions.

These come from upstream `spa/utils/type-info.h` / `spa/buffer/buffer.h` enum `spa_data_type`.

Add them to `pipewire-native-spa` (likely `spa/src/param/` or a new `spa/src/data.rs` or `spa/src/buffer.rs`). Then server re-exports from spa.
acceptance_criteria:
- `spa_data_type` constants live in `pipewire-native-spa`
- server uses `pipewire_native_spa::...::spa_data_type::*`
- Constants deleted from `server/src/protocol/messages.rs`
notes: Reparented under SU-client-node-cycle because canonical memory kinds directly gate AddMem interpretation. Delegated to update SPA, server, and node with one source of truth.
close_reason: Completed in 12dc2df5: canonical SPA DataType definitions, server compatibility re-export, corrected node MEM_FD=2/DMA_BUF=3 conversion, and ABI/conversion tests.

title: Add shared POD encode_struct / parse_struct helpers to spa crate
description:
Server defines two helpers that are general-purpose POD utilities:
- `encode_struct_payload()` — wraps `Builder::new().push_struct(build).build()` with a fixed 8192 buffer
- `parse_struct()` — wraps `Parser::new().pop_struct(parse)` with error mapping

These would be useful in spa/ as convenience functions. Add them to `spa/src/pod/` (new `helpers.rs` or extend existing builder/parser).

Consider whether the 8192 fixed buffer is appropriate or should be configurable.
acceptance_criteria:
- `encode_struct` and `parse_struct` exist in `pipewire-native-spa::pod`
- server uses the shared versions
- private `encode_struct_payload` and `parse_struct` deleted from server
close_reason: Not pursued as part of the ClientNode tracer bullet. Fixed-size convenience wrappers would be shallow and the shared protocol migration does not require them; revisit only with a concrete reusable caller.

title: Evaluate shared SCM_RIGHTS I/O helpers
description:
Both server and client implement SCM_RIGHTS recvmsg/sendmsg but with different I/O models:
- Server: per-packet atomic reads (read header, then read_exact payload)
- Client: streaming buffered reads into a growable buffer

Unifying requires extracting the low-level cmsg construction/parsing while keeping the read model separate. Candidates for sharing:
- `parse_received_fds(msg: &msghdr)` — identical logic
- cmsg construction for sendmsg — identical logic

This is a design evaluation ticket. Assess whether the abstraction boundary is clean enough to justify a shared module, or if the coupling to different I/O strategies makes it not worth it.
acceptance_criteria:
- Decision documented on whether to unify
- If yes: shared functions created in pipewire/ or spa/
- If no: rationale documented
close_reason: Completed by /.design/native-frame/frame0.gpt56.md and shared pipewire-native-protocol implementation: one bounded frame/FD seam with ownership, partial IO, cleanup, migration, and adversarial tests.
